kept.spine: Anyone with goods to sell can take a place in the market here, and the stalls sit where the carts come off the road.
Rules here have rooms. A matter goes to the hall, the courthouse or the customs house before it goes to a person, and each of the three keeps its own hours.
People here can afford to argue about something other than money.
The town pays for itself, and no part of its keeping rests on luck.
The walls are sound, the watch is kept, and nothing in either was built for show.
Nobody here expects the town to lose a straight fight, and the town speaks to its neighbours on that footing.
Beasts on this ground are an ordinary matter, and the town answers them with a charter hall, bowyers and a watch that knows the work.
Order here keeps to the main streets, and what happens in the lanes behind them is the lanes' own business.
Prices here hold from one market day to the next, and no trade in the town is living on its last sale.
The town's own magic runs to an alchemist's shop and a lamp at the gate, and anything past that is sent for from outside.
The price of bread is watched here, and the households that watch it are not short of money.
The Governing Council and the Order of the Watch are careful with each other, and what they are careful about is political influence.
The traffic on the road is real, and the town takes very little of its living from it.
The road brings what the town cannot grow, and the town has no second way to be fed.
Spitzplatz is a town in the ordinary sense of the word, and the word covers it.
One tie here carries more weight than the rest, and it is an unpaid debt that the town takes care not to disturb.
Ties between people here run on the ordinary things, work and family and living a long time on the same street.
